## QUESTION 1

```{python}
# Include and execute your code here
removed = df.with_columns(
  pl.col("month").replace("n/a", None),
  pl.col("num_of_delays_carrier").replace("1500+", None).cast(pl.Int64),
  pl.col("num_of_delays_late_aircraft").replace(-999, None),
  pl.col("minutes_delayed_nas").replace(-999, None),
  pl.col("airport_name").replace("", None)
)
```
```{python}
print(removed.slice(0,1).write_json())
```
## QUESTION 2

2. __Filling in missing data__ For all the "minutes_delayed" columns, fill in any missing values with the median of that column. For the "num_of" columns, fill in missing values with that column's mean.

_Nothing to write/report for this question_

```{python}
filled = removed.with_columns(
  pl.col("minutes_delayed_nas").fill_null(pl.col("minutes_delayed_nas").median()),
  pl.col(["num_of_delays_carrier", "num_of_delays_late_aircraft"]).fill_null(strategy="mean")
)
```

## QUESTION 3
 
3. __Display a histogram for num_of_delays_carrier and for minutes_delayed_nas (2 separate histograms in total). Comment on the shape of each one. Also report the mean of each of these columns now that missing values have been filled in.__

Carrier delays are well spread out in their amounts with all values having a gradual downward trend starting with a lower number of delays decreasing towards larger numbers the interesting thing is there is a massive spike at 696.6 delays which is extremely close to the mean number of carrier delays of 691.27 delays.

On the other hand with the NAS delays the large majority of delays are on the smaller side with the most common length of a delay being 18,790.5 minutes but the major difference between this set and the Carrier Delays is that the drastic outliers present in the data has caused the mean number of minutes delayed to be 69682.66 minutes.
